info.title: EmailFig API
info.description:
Keep contacts, lists, tags and custom fields in sync with your own app, place signup forms, and read how your campaigns performed.

**Authentication.** Create a key under Settings > API keys and send it as `Authorization: Bearer emf_live_...`. Call `GET /account` to check that a key works.

**Pagination.** Contacts, tags and campaigns come back in pages of 25, or up to 100 with `per_page` (larger values are capped at 100). When there is more, `meta.next_cursor` is set: send it back as `cursor`, with the same filters, for the next page. It is `null` on the last page. Lists, custom fields and forms come back whole.

**Rate limit.** 300 requests per five minutes per key. Past that you get a `429` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

**Errors.** Failures are RFC 7807 problem documents (`application/problem+json`). The last part of `type` is a stable code, so check that rather than the wording of `title` or `detail`. Every code is explained at https://emailfig.com/docs/errors. Any endpoint can answer `500` with `server_error` if something goes wrong on our side.

Questions? Email contact@emailfig.com and a real person will reply.

get.description: The simplest way to check that an API key works. It succeeds even on a brand-new account with nothing in it.

Newest first. Filters combine. `email` and `tag` match the whole value, ignoring case. `list_id` matches anyone with a membership on that list, whatever its status; read `lists` for the status.

To sync changes, pass `updated_since`. Contacts then come back oldest change first, and a contact that changes while you are paging comes round again at the end. Start your next sync a minute before the `updated_at` of the last contact you read: a change is stamped when it is written, and a long write such as an import can finish after later ones, so the overlap is what catches it. Expect to see a few contacts twice. Any change counts, including an unsubscribe, a bounce, or a change to the contact's lists or tags. Renaming a tag does not count as a change to the contacts that carry it.

Deleted contacts are left out unless you pass `include_deleted=true`.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Exact address. A blank value matches no contact.

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description: An ISO 8601 time, such as `2026-09-18T12:00:00Z`; with no offset it is read as UTC. Returns contacts changed at or after it. A value that can't be read is rejected with a `422`.

parameters.name: include_deleted
parameters.description: Include deleted contacts. Each has `deleted_at` set. Erased contacts are gone for good and never appear.

post.summary: Create or update a contact
post.description:
If a contact with this email address exists, it is updated, and a deleted one is restored. Otherwise one is created. You get `201` for a new contact and `200` for an update. A new contact for an address that unsubscribed or bounced before, including one that was erased, starts `unsubscribed` or `cleaned` rather than `subscribed`.

Fields you send replace what is stored, and fields you leave out are kept. A blank `first_name`, `last_name` or `source` is treated as left out. In `properties`, send `null` or an empty string to clear a value; see `CustomField` for the format each type takes. `tags` are added to the contact's existing tags.

This doesn't add the contact to a list. Use `POST /lists/{list_id}/contacts` for that.

properties.description: Custom field values, keyed by field key. Each field must already exist, and each value must fit its type and be at most 255 characters.

tags.description: A name over 100 characters is a `422` with the code `too_long`, and nothing is written.

patch.description: Works like `POST /contacts`, and can also change the email address. An address another contact already has is rejected with the code `contact_exists`.

properties.description: Custom field values, keyed by field key, each at most 255 characters.

tags.description: A name over 100 characters is a `422` with the code `too_long`, and nothing is written.

delete.description:
Permanently erases the contact and their details from EmailFig, for a right-to-erasure request. It works on a deleted contact too. This can't be undone. If they had unsubscribed, that is kept, so the address can't be emailed even if it is added again. An id that is already erased returns `404`, so a retry can treat that as done.

To stop emailing someone without erasing them, use `POST /contacts/{id}/unsubscribe`.

post.summary: Unsubscribe a contact
post.description: Stops all email to the contact, for when they opt out somewhere else, such as in your app or at checkout. They are kept, so importing the same address again won't resubscribe them. If they sign up again through `POST /lists/{list_id}/contacts`, they get a confirmation email and are back once they click it.

post.summary: Unsubscribe an email address
post.description: Stops all email to an address, whether or not it belongs to a contact yet, so a later signup or import can't subscribe it. A contact with the address, including a deleted one, is marked unsubscribed and returned; `contact` is null when there is none.

200.description: The address, and its contact if there is one.

post.summary: Add a contact to a list
post.description:
Adds the contact to the list, creating the contact first if needed. This is the one way to add someone to a list, so use it for signups from your own forms too.

If the list uses double opt-in, the contact gets a confirmation email and joins once they click it. So does anyone who unsubscribed or was deleted before, whatever the list's setting. Until then a new membership shows in `lists` as `pending`, and one they already had keeps its status. A new contact's own `status` is `pending` too, and so is a deleted one's unless they had unsubscribed. There's no way to skip confirmation from the request.

For a contact who already exists, the fields you send replace what is stored and the ones you leave out are kept, as with `POST /contacts`. A blank `first_name` or `last_name` counts as left out. `source` is only set when the contact is created.

Adding someone who is already subscribed to the list won't add them twice or email them again, so it's safe to retry. Retrying for someone still confirming sends the confirmation again, at most once every 10 minutes.

source.description: Where the signup came from, such as `wordpress:comment_form`.

properties.description: Custom field values, keyed by field key. Each field must already exist, and each value must fit its type and be at most 255 characters.

tags.description: Tags to add once the contact is on the list. A contact still confirming isn't enrolled in automations by them.

422.description: The contact couldn't be added. The code in `type` says why: `validation_failed` (a field was rejected, see `errors`), `address_unmailable` (the address has a complaint, a bounce or a suppression on record, is marked undeliverable, or is on a disposable email domain), or `confirmation_unavailable` (the signup needs a confirmation email, which the account can't send until a sending domain is set up).

delete.summary: Remove a contact from a list
delete.description: Takes the contact off this list, including a join still waiting on its confirmation, and leaves their other lists alone. If they unsubscribed from this list themselves, that is kept, and the list stays in `lists` as `unsubscribed`. A confirmation email already sent still works: if they click it, they join.

200.description: A page of tags, in name order.

post.summary: Tag a contact

tags.description: A name over 100 characters is a `422` with the code `too_long`, and nothing is written.

delete.description: Removes every named tag from the contact. Names match in any case. A name with no tag in the account, or one the contact doesn't carry, is skipped, so the call is safe to retry. Send the names in the body or as `tags[]` query parameters.

post.summary: Create a custom field
post.description: `key` is converted to lowercase with underscores, and can't be changed later. `email_address`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `status` and `source` are built-in contact fields and can't be used as keys. An account can have at most 30 custom fields; creating another is rejected with a `422` whose error has the field `base` and the code `limit_reached`.

options.description: Required for a `choice` field: 2 to 50 options.

patch.description: Changes `label`, `field_type` or a `choice` field's `options`. Sending the field's own `key` back is fine; a different one is rejected, since keys can't change. A new `field_type` is rejected if a value already stored wouldn't fit it, and a field can't change into or out of `choice`.

delete.description: Rejected while a signup form that isn't archived still asks for this field.

get.description: Draft and live forms, in name order. Archived forms are left out.
Works for a form of any status, archived included.

post.summary: Create a webhook endpoint
post.description: The response carries `secret`, the signing secret, once. An endpoint created here belongs to the API key that created it: revoking the key deletes it, and a `410` from the receiver deletes it. An account can have 20 of these; the 21st is refused with code `limit_reached` on `base`. The URL must be https on the standard port, and one another endpoint in the account uses is refused with code `taken` on `url`.

201.description: The new endpoint, with its secret.

patch.description: Fields you send replace what is stored; fields you leave out are kept. `enabled: false` turns the endpoint off, and `enabled: true` turns it back on and resets its failures. Any other `enabled` value is refused with code `invalid` on `enabled`.

204.description: Deleted. Nothing more is sent to it.

get.summary: Recent examples of an event type
get.description: Up to 3 events rebuilt from the account's newest matching records, in exactly the shape a delivery carries, for a connector's sample step. Writes and sends nothing. `list_id` is required for `contact.list_subscribed` and `contact.list_unsubscribed`, `tag_id` for `contact.tag_added` and `contact.tag_removed`; `form_id` optionally narrows `form.submitted`. The two removal types pair recent contacts with the chosen list or tag.

post.summary: Send a test event
post.description: Sends one `webhook.test` event through the real delivery path, to check the endpoint answers. Its `data` is empty, so trigger a real event (add a test contact, say) to get fields to map. Refused while the endpoint is off.

bearerAuth.description: An API key from Settings > API keys. It starts with `emf_live_`.

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: The `meta.next_cursor` from the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

from_email.description: The address your email is sent from. Empty until one is set up.

key_name.description: The name of the API key you called with.

status.description: `pending` is waiting on a confirmation email. `cleaned` means the address can't receive email: it bounced, or an import marked it.

properties.description: Custom field values, keyed by the field's `key`.

lists.description: Every list the contact has joined, left, or is still confirming. The contact's own `status` still decides whether they get email at all.

deleted_at.description: When the contact was deleted, or `null`. `GET /contacts` returns deleted contacts only when you ask for `include_deleted=true`, and a `contact.deleted` event carries one.

status.description: `pending` is waiting on the double opt-in confirmation. `unsubscribed` means they left this list.

double_optin.description: When true, someone added to this list gets a confirmation email and joins once they click it.

subscribed_count.description: Contacts on the list who can be emailed.

Consent.description: Details of the person's opt-in, kept as a record of consent. Send these when you are passing on a signup that happened somewhere else, such as a form on your site; otherwise the record shows your server's IP and the time of this request.

ip.description: The person's IPv4 or IPv6 address. A value that isn't an IP address is not stored.

at.description: When they opted in, in ISO 8601; a time with no offset is read as UTC. Worth sending if the request might be delayed, such as a retry or a signup waiting on approval.

key.description: The name its value is stored under in `properties`.

field_type.description: What a value must look like. `text` takes any value. `number` takes a whole number, as a number or a string such as `"42"`; `12.5` is rejected. `date` takes `YYYY-MM-DD`, and a time after it is ignored. `boolean` takes `true` or `false`, and also `"yes"`/`"no"` and `"1"`/`"0"`. `choice` takes one of the field's `options`, matched without regard to case and stored in the option's own spelling. A value that doesn't fit is rejected with a `422`, and so is any value longer than 255 characters (code `too_long`, on the field `properties.<key>`).

options.description: A `choice` field's options, 2 to 50, in the order a form shows them, each different from the others. Empty for every other type. Removing an option leaves the contacts that hold it as they are.

kind.description: An `embed` shows where you place it. A `popup` chooses its own pages from its settings in EmailFig, so place it once per site, in the page head. A `landing_page` is its own page, at `public_url`, and can't be placed on a site.

status.description: Only a `live` form shows on a site. A paused one that has been placed shows nothing.

double_optin.description: Whether the form's list uses double opt-in. Change it on the list.

script_url.description: The script to load the form with.

public_url.description: The page's address, for a `landing_page`. Null for other kinds.

stats.description: Null until the campaign starts sending.

recipients.description: How many people the campaign was addressed to.

sent.description: Emails sent so far. Divide `delivered` by this for the delivery rate.

next_cursor.description: Send this as `cursor` to get the next page. `null` when this is the last page.

type.description: A link to the error's documentation. Its last part is the code, and every code is listed at https://emailfig.com/docs/errors.

errors.description: On a validation failure, one entry for each field that was rejected.

enabled.description: Whether events are sent to it. Events from while it is off are not kept, and turning it off drops its deliveries not yet made.

disabled_reason.description: `user` if someone turned it off, `breaker` if every attempt failed for 24 hours, `gone` if an endpoint made in Settings answered `410` (one made through the API is deleted instead).

key_owned.description: Created through the API, so it belongs to that API key.

WebhookEventBatch.description: Every request body is an array of 1 to 100 events, in no guaranteed order (order by each event's `timestamp`), under 512 KB unless one event alone is larger. One body can mix event types.

id.description: The same on every retry, and for every endpoint that receives the event. Dedupe on it. Opaque: don't sort by it.

anyOf.description: Sent only by Send test event; its `data` is empty.

timestamp.description: When the change was written, to the microsecond. Order by this and apply last-write-wins.

origin.description: Who made the change: a person in the app, an API key, the contact (a form, a confirmation, preferences or an unsubscribe), or EmailFig itself. It does not say which API client. To ignore your own write-backs, mark them (for example with a custom field) or use find-or-create; skipping every `api` event also drops other integrations' writes.

data.description: `contact` on every `contact.*` event and on `form.submitted`. List events add `list`, tag events add `tag`, and `form.submitted` adds `form`. `campaign.sent` carries `campaign` alone, and `webhook.test` carries nothing. Each record is as it was when the event was sent, seconds after the change, so it can already show a later one: the `type` says what happened, the record says where things stand.

campaign.description: Delivery counts at completion. Opens and clicks are not included; they keep arriving for days.

Unauthorized.description: The API key is missing, wrong, or revoked.

ValidationError.description: Something in the request was rejected. `errors` says which field and why.

Forbidden.description: The account is being deleted (`account_closing`) or is suspended (`account_suspended`), so every request is refused. Retrying won't help.

BadRequest.description: The request body isn't valid JSON.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then try again.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: The account your API key belongs to.

tags.name: Contacts
tags.description: The people you send to. `POST /contacts` creates a contact or updates the one with that email address, so you never need to check first. Adding someone to a list is done from the Lists endpoints.

tags.name: Lists
tags.description: The lists you send to, and who is on them. Adding a contact to a list counts as a signup: if the list uses double opt-in, or the contact had unsubscribed before, they get a confirmation email and join once they click it.

tags.name: Tags
tags.description: Labels for your contacts. Adding a tag that doesn't exist yet creates it.

tags.name: Custom fields
tags.description: Extra fields you store on contacts, such as a company or a plan. They apply to your whole account, not to one list. Define a field here before you send a value for it; the values themselves are read and written as `properties` on a contact.

tags.name: Forms
tags.description: The signup forms you built in EmailFig. To place one on a site, add `<script async src="{script_url}" data-form="{id}"></script>`. Changes you make to the form in EmailFig show up everywhere it is placed.

tags.name: Campaigns
tags.description: What you have sent, and how it performed.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Endpoints we POST events to as your contacts change. Each request body is a JSON array of 1 to 100 events, which can mix types, signed with Standard Webhooks (`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature`). `webhook-id` names the request; each event's `id` is the same on every retry, and for every endpoint that receives the event. Delivery is at-least-once and unordered: dedupe on each event's `id`, and apply each event's `timestamp` last-write-wins. A failing delivery is retried for 24 hours, and an endpoint where every attempt has failed for 24 hours is turned off. Answer `410 Gone` to stop: an endpoint made in Settings is turned off, one made through the API is deleted. Every event carries `origin`: whether a person (`ui`), an API key (`api`), the contact (`recipient`) or EmailFig itself (`system`) made the change. It does not say which API client. `contact.updated` fires only when a value really changes, so writing back the values an event carried cannot loop. An integration that writes back and must ignore its own writes should mark them (for example with a custom field it sets) or use find-or-create, rather than drop every `api` event, which would also drop other integrations' writes, such as WordPress plugin signups. Changes from CSV imports are never sent.

**What sends nothing.** Erasing a contact (`DELETE /contacts/{id}`) sends no event, and its events not yet sent are dropped. Deleting a list or tag sends no leave or remove events for its contacts, and renaming one sends nothing, so key on `data.list.id` and `data.tag.id` rather than names. A change to a contact's `source` alone sends no `contact.updated`.

**Answering a request.** Answer any `2xx` to acknowledge every event in it, then do the work: we wait 2 seconds to connect, 5 seconds for the response and 10 seconds in all. Redirects are not followed, so a `3xx` counts as a failure, like any other status. Answer `410 Gone` to stop: an endpoint made in Settings is turned off, one made through the API is deleted. `429` is retried on the same schedule as a failure, never sooner than its `Retry-After` header (seconds or an HTTP date), and does not count toward turning the endpoint off. To catch up after an endpoint was off, read `GET /contacts?updated_since=<time>&include_deleted=true`; the endpoint's page in EmailFig shows the time to use.

**Compatibility.** New event types, new fields and new enum values (such as another `origin` or `status`) can appear without notice, so ignore what you don't recognise. An endpoint only receives the event types it lists. Existing fields are not removed or renamed without notice. Keys can arrive in any order, and ids are opaque: don't sort by them.
